title: Powers of ell act invertibly on derived continuous field coefficients
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite normed extension, and let $X$ be any scheme. Let $E_X=p_X^*\underline E$ be the actual continuous coefficient ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use internal module objects and their ordinary unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For every $K\in D(\Mod_{E_X})$ and every integer $n\geq0$, the endomorphism $\ell^n\operatorname{id}_K$ is invertible. The inverse is induced on a complex representative by the action of the constant coefficient $\ell^{-n}\in E$.

source.place: F inverts W: multiplication by ell on rational coefficients is invertible

proof.text: Write m = ell^n. Define an endomorphism t of the actual condensed abelian sheaf underlying E by sending each continuous function f on a profinite S to the function (ell^n)^(-1) f. This is continuous, additive and natural under precomposition. The field E has characteristic zero because it is a Q_ell-algebra; hence ell^n is nonzero. Evaluating pointwise shows m times t = id. The point inverse image F = p_X^* is a left adjoint between abelian sheaf categories, so it preserves binary coproducts and zero morphisms, hence biproducts and addition. Consequently m times F(t) = id on E_X.

source.place: F inverts W, sentence: ell acts invertibly on E_X-modules; explicit inverse using additivity and the module unit axiom

proof.text: For an internal A-module M and an endomorphism v of A satisfying m times v = id, form b = lambda_M^(-1); ((eta_A;v) tensor id_M); gamma_M on the underlying object. Additivity of tensoring and composition, followed by the unit action axiom, gives m times b = id_M. Thus b is a two-sided inverse of m times id on the underlying object: both composites equal m times b. The forgetful functor from internal modules reflects isomorphisms, since the inverse of an action-compatible isomorphism is action-compatible by cancellation. Therefore m times id_M is an isomorphism of modules, and uniqueness of its underlying inverse identifies that inverse with b. Apply this to A=E_X and v=F(t). This argument uses no centrality or additional coefficient comparison.

source.place: F inverts W, sentence: ell acts invertibly on E_X-modules; explicit inverse using additivity and the module unit axiom

proof.text: By the ordinary unbounded derived localization's essential surjectivity choose C and e:Q(C) isomorphic to K. Apply step 2 in every degree to see that m times id_C is a componentwise isomorphism and hence an isomorphism of complexes. Put B = inverse(m times id_C); functoriality of evaluation and step 2 give exactly the asserted formula for B in each degree. The additive localization satisfies Q(m times id_C)=m times id_Q(C). Functoriality preserves both inverse equations for B. Conjugating Q(B) by e gives the displayed two-sided inverse of m times id_K, and hence its IsIso instance. Every degree is allowed, with no boundedness hypothesis.
